description: A ref:// link in a message opens the code it points at, snapshotted when the message was sent.
agent_instructions: Switchboard renders ref:// links as a code viewer. LABEL THEM AS CODE. The link label is `filename : symbol`, e.g. [refFile.ts : loadRefFile], which the console renders as a non-breaking chip with a code icon rather than as prose. The label is a LABEL: do not restate the whole scope chain in it, that lives in the destination, and do not write a prose phrase, which hides that the link points into code. Write a markdown link whose destination is ref://path/to/file.ts, optionally followed by :Scope:Name waypoints and an optional #matcher; the file is snapshotted at send time and attached, so the reader sees the code as it was when you wrote about it. Only the `full` field of channel_reply and notify_human is scanned; a ref in summary, title, fullSpoken, or a crosstalk_send body arrives as a link that cannot open. PATHS RESOLVE THE WAY A SHELL READS THEM: a bare path is relative to the project (src/cart.ts), a leading / is the filesystem root, and ~/ is the owner's home. Prefer the bare project-relative form; reach for / or ~/ when the file is genuinely outside the project, or when this session was launched somewhere other than the repo it is working in, which makes a bare path resolve against the wrong directory. A ref naming a secret (anything under .ssh/.gnupg/.aws/.docker/.kube, a .env, a .pem or other key file) is refused and FAILS the send: quote the part you mean instead. Waypoints match any descendant, so ref://app.tsx:App:handleSubmit works through unnamed layers. A qualified name may be written either way: :Acme.Services or :Acme:Services, and A::B::method or A:B:method. Qualify fully when you can, since a partial chain can resolve to a narrower range. Use :arguments for a parameter list and :arguments:name for one parameter. Matchers: #text highlights the first match inside the resolved scope; #text@before:anchor and #text@after:anchor pick the occurrence nearest before or after another string; #from..to spans a range. ENCODING. A matcher is code, and a link destination ends at the first space or unbalanced ) , which silently truncates the ref rather than reporting anything. Either percent-encode (%20 for a space, %29 for a close paren, and %2E%2E or %40 for a literal .. or @ that would otherwise read as a range or an anchor), or simply wrap the whole destination in angle brackets, which is easier: [label](<ref://src/cart.ts:Cart:add#items.push(item);>). WHAT FAILS AND WHAT DOES NOT. The file tier fails the send loudly, naming the ref: missing, not text, a refused secret, too large to snapshot without narrowing. A malformed ref also fails, with the offset. But RESOLUTION never fails: if a scope chain no longer matches, the ref still sends and the viewer opens on a text match or the whole file with a banner, and nothing tells you it missed. So no error does NOT mean the ref pointed where you intended; a near-miss scheme like ref:/file.ts is simply not recognised as a ref at all and is skipped in silence. A ref inside a code fence or inline code is never detected, so documenting this format costs nothing.
